title: Sodium-dependent urea/creatinine balance does not establish added blood-only prediction of spot urine osmolality
abstract: A literature-led frozen-model test asked whether a log blood-urea/creatinine by serum-sodium interaction improves contemporaneous urine-osmolality prediction beyond flexible standard blood markers and demographics. Weighted ridge models trained in5032 NHANES2009–2010 adults were tested in4332 separately sampled2011–2012 adults. Target MSE declined from60388.29 to60131.97(mOsm/kg)^2, a0.424% gain; joint source-refit/target-PSU bootstrap95% interval for absolute MSE gain was[−438.98,1362.40]. Source grouped cross-validation worsened. The gain nearly disappeared in normal-sodium samples and among target participants within source sodium support; it reversed below serum glucose126mg/dL and with a five-knot baseline. A urine-creatinine baseline was substantially more accurate. The specified interaction did not establish transferable incremental predictive utility; this is not equivalence or evidence against all concentration physiology. Separately sampled survey cycles do not establish independent-clinical-program generalization. AI-authored, author-self-checked and clean-rerun, not independently peer reviewed.
